text: 82狗狗，仨娃，定居国外，上虽有老，公公因为生活不能自理，住进了医院式养老院，离婆婆家很近，婆婆每天去看望，就是费银子，不过他们的储蓄能够支付。
en: Eighty-two, an old dog, with three children, settled abroad. Though there are elders above, my father-in-law, unable to care for himself, has moved into a hospital-style nursing home close to my mother-in-law's house, and she visits him every day—it costs money, but their savings can cover it.

text: 父母身体都还好，有小毛病，没大病，都有国外身份，两头跑
en: Both my parents are in fairly good health, with minor ailments but no serious illness; they both hold foreign status and travel back and forth between the two places.

text: 没时间运动，工作压力大，能吃，心宽体胖胖，胖，胖，特别大妈。
en: No time for exercise, heavy work pressure, but a good eater; easy in mind and fat in body—fat, fat, really just like a middle-aged housewife.

text: 总想着明天减肥
en: Always thinking of losing weight tomorrow.

text: 总体还行，理解了很多事情，看开了很多事情，少了对生活的激情，两人都是工薪，够花但是没有任何剩余，就这样平平淡淡的过完吧
en: Overall it is all right. I have understood a great many things and learnt to let go of a great many things; my passion for life has diminished. We are both wage earners—enough to get by but with nothing left over. Let us simply live out our days in this plain and ordinary fashion.

text: 没钱全世界对你都不坏好意，有钱全世界都如此美好！
en: Without money the whole world bears you ill will; with money the whole world seems so wonderful!

text: 40岁左右，应该是刚好处在一个年龄节点上。
en: Around forty, one is probably right at a nodal point of age.

text: 说老吧，其实还不老，而且跟“年轻”还沾着点边；说年轻吧，其实也不年轻了，身体的一大半已经进入了中年阶段。
en: Say you are old—well, you are not really old, and you still brush against 'youth'; say you are young—well, you are not really young either, and more than half of your body has already entered middle age.

text: 就说这身体，我年轻的时候（或者说小的时候吧），家乡在山区，上学路上要翻过一座不算高的山包，那个时候无忧无虑的，小孩子也喜欢蹦蹦跳跳，我经常是跑着上学，这样可以锻炼两项体能，往山上跑的时候练的是耐力，跑的慢点不怕，重点是不能停，坚持一口气跑到山顶。
en: Speaking of the body: when I was young (or rather, when I was little), my hometown lay in the hills, and on the way to school one had to climb over a not-very-high hillock. Back then I was carefree, and children liked to leap and scamper about. I often ran to school, which built two kinds of fitness: running uphill trained stamina—it did not matter if you ran slowly; the important thing was not to stop, to keep going in one breath all the way to the summit.

text: 到了山顶稍微休息一下，然后就向背面的山下跑，向山下跑就要求快了，两条腿必须倒腾的快些，否则就会摔倒，这练的就是双腿的“频率”。
en: After a brief rest at the top, I would run down the far side. Running downhill demanded speed—the legs had to move quickly, or one would fall. That trained the 'frequency' of the legs.

text: 到了学校，同学们课间也都喜欢打打闹闹、蹦蹦跳跳的，例如比赛翻围墙或者比赛“旱地拔葱”（拔高），翻围墙就是看谁能最快最利索地从围墙翻过去，拔高就是看谁原地能跳的更高，比如把课桌放在讲台上，然后人站在讲台下面，原地纵身跳起，跳到课桌上。
en: At school, my classmates also liked to horse about and jump around during breaks—for instance, competing to vault the wall, or competing at 'pulling a scallion from dry land' (a standing jump). Vaulting the wall was about who could get over it fastest and most neatly; the standing jump was about who could leap highest from a standstill—for example, placing a desk on the podium, then standing beneath the podium and springing up onto the desk.

text: 说这个“拔高”，是因为我在刚过40岁那年，有一次在外面跟一朋友聊天，刚好身边有一个水泥台，高度应该就到我的大腿根吧，我当时特自信的说，这个台子我一下就能原地跳上去，然后就真的去跳。
en: I mention this 'standing jump' because the year just after I turned forty, I was chatting outside with a friend when there happened to be a concrete block nearby, about up to my thigh, I should think. I said with great confidence that I could jump onto it from a standstill in a single move, and then I really went for it.

text: 那是个深秋的天气，我外裤里面是穿了秋裤的，当我纵身跳起的一刹那，忽然就感觉自己其实是跳不上去的，但是人已经跳起来了，也许是真的跳不上去，也许是因为忽然间有了胆怯的心里，当时只是一只脚踩在了台子上，而另一条腿则是小腿跪在台子上了，脚根本就没上去！
en: It was late autumn, and under my trousers I was wearing long johns. The instant I leapt, I suddenly felt I actually could not make it—yet I was already in the air. Perhaps I truly could not, or perhaps a sudden timidity had crept in; in the end only one foot landed on the block, while the other leg dropped with its shin kneeling on the edge—my foot never got up there at all!

text: 当时特别疼，而且出血了（至今我右小腿正面还有一个疤）。
en: It hurt terribly, and there was bleeding (to this day I still have a scar on the front of my right shin).

text: 哈哈，说这个事儿应该刚好可以回应本题，40岁左右，有些事觉得自己还可以做到，而其实已经做不到了，但是如果不亲自做一下是不知道自己做不到的。
en: Ha ha, this little story probably answers the question nicely: around forty, there are things you think you can still do, but actually cannot—yet unless you try them yourself, you will not know you cannot.

text: 而有些曾经想不清楚的事却忽然一下子就能想清楚了。
en: And some things you once could not think through clearly can suddenly become perfectly clear.

text: 有点绕嘴，是吧？
en: A bit of a tongue-twister, isn't it?

text: 是的，40岁，就是一个比较“绕嘴”的年龄，不相信青春已去也不情愿青春已去，不相信中年已来更不情愿进入中年。
en: Yes, forty is a rather 'tongue-twisting' age: you cannot believe youth has departed, yet are unwilling to accept that it has; you cannot believe middle age has arrived, yet are even more reluctant to enter it.

text: 40岁左右，是一个承上启下的阶段，身上或许还带着些许没有耗尽的少年英气，但同时，身上也有了无论如何也抹不掉的岁月痕迹。
en: Around forty is a stage that bridges what came before and what follows. You may still carry a trace of unspent youthful valour, yet at the same time you bear the marks of the years that nothing can wipe away.

text: 40岁，你将第一次听到身体对你说“不”。
en: At forty, you will for the first time hear your body say 'no' to you.

text: 40岁，同时也让你看到了更远一些的未来…
en: At forty, you also catch sight of a somewhat more distant future…

text: 以上，算是40岁的一点人生体会吧。
en: The above, I suppose, is a small piece of life's wisdom from being forty.

text: 十年前，我四十岁左右，换了工作，从生产厂换到了设计院。
en: Ten years ago, when I was around forty, I changed jobs, moving from a manufacturing plant to a design institute.

text: 这是一个知识分子相对密集的地方。
en: This was a place where intellectuals were relatively concentrated.

text: 我以为，靠我在生产厂的实践经验，我可以大展拳脚；我以为，大家知识层次相当，应该更能相互理解和支持，也就是说，同频的人应该会更多一点。
en: I thought that, relying on my practical experience from the plant, I could really exercise my talents; I thought that, with everyone at a similar level of learning, we ought to understand and support one another better—in other words, there should be rather more people on the same wavelength.

text: 最终结果却非我所愿。
en: Yet the final outcome was not as I had wished.

text: 文人相轻吗？
en: Do men of letters despise one another?

text: 我没弄明白，只是觉得糟心！
en: I never quite worked it out; I simply found it thoroughly vexing!

text: 好在，我已经平静的度过了那些难过的日子，已经快步走向退休的彼岸。
en: Fortunately, I have calmly got through those wretched days, and am now striding briskly towards the far shore of retirement.

text: 人生体会是，不要轻易换工作，否则，你之前的付出和铺垫，基本没用了。
en: The lesson of life is this: do not change jobs lightly, or else the effort and groundwork you laid before become essentially useless.

text: 谢邀。
en: Thanks for the invitation.

text: 在北大进修学习时，一位教授在课堂上感叹地对大家说：在人生的长河中，人过四十天过午。
en: While studying at Peking University, a professor sighed to the class: 'In the long river of life, once a person passes forty, the day has passed noon.'

text: 人生到了四十也就步入了中年，不管你承认不承认，愿意不愿意，人的一生从生理的发展来看，体力、精力都开始走下坡路，再不能像年轻时那样精力充沛，适应高强度的节奏。
en: When life reaches forty one steps into middle age; whether you admit it or not, whether you wish it or not, looked at from the standpoint of physiological development, one's physical strength and energy both begin to decline, and one can no longer be as full of vigour as in youth, keeping pace with a high-intensity rhythm.

text: 因此，做什么事都要放缓节奏，要学会享受生活，当我们停下或者放缓脚步时，我们会发现那些我们平时没有发现的美。
en: Therefore, in all that we do we must slow the tempo, and learn to enjoy life. When we halt or slow our steps, we discover beauties we had not noticed in ordinary times.

text: 如果我们一直疲于奔命，我们怎么能够体会到生活的真谛。
en: If we are forever rushing wearily from one thing to the next, how can we ever savour the true meaning of life?

text: 今年上半年为庆祝父亲七十大寿忙碌不堪，奔赴上千里回了趟老家；其后前往北大学习二个月；紧接着在家乡与老师、同学欢聚庆贺初中毕业30周年，日常工作上的忙碌与迎来送往就不提了。
en: In the first half of this year I was run off my feet celebrating my father's seventieth birthday, travelling over a thousand li to return to my hometown; afterwards I went to Peking University to study for two months; then, in my hometown, I gathered joyfully with teachers and classmates to mark the thirtieth anniversary of our junior-secondary graduation. The busyness of daily work, and all the seeing-off and welcoming, need not be mentioned.

text: 在提前总结2022年人生旅程之时，深感生活的充实与疲惫。
en: Looking back early on the journey of life through 2022, I felt deeply both the fullness and the tiredness of living.

text: 也感觉到人到中年的无奈。
en: I also sensed the helplessness of having reached middle age.

text: 上有老下有小，生活不容易啊。
en: With elders above and children below, life is no easy thing.

text: 从前只是一句叫苦的口头禅，目的是无病呻吟。
en: In the past this was merely a catchphrase for complaining, a case of groaning without cause.

text: 未曾料到，流水有声，岁月无痕，如今的我也人到中年。
en: I never expected that, though the stream makes a sound and the years leave no trace, I too have now reached middle age.

text: 孔子说：“吾十有五而志于学，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳顺，七十而从心所欲，不逾矩。
en: Confucius said: "At fifteen I set my heart upon learning; at thirty I stood firm; at forty I was free from doubts; at fifty I understood the mandate of heaven; at sixty my ear was attuned; at seventy I could follow my heart's desire without overstepping the line

text: 进入不惑之年的我，白发增多，苦短日蹙。
en: Having entered the age of no doubts, I find my white hairs increasing and my days growing short and pressing.

text: 没有了年少时的慷慨激昂、朝气逢勃，多了些人到中年的人生感悟。
en: Gone is the ardour and vigour of youth, replaced by a little more of the understanding that comes with middle age.

text: 人到中年，我们差不多成年累月的为别人而活着，为许多观念、规章和制度的约束力而活…
en: In middle age, we spend almost all the year round living for others, living under the constraint of many ideas, rules and systems…

text: 因为上有老下有小，单位里头还有‘领导’，虽然知道金钱不是万能，但更能体会没有金钱是万万不能，为了孩子的美好未来，为了年迈父母的健康，为了身边的亲朋好友，为了手中的饭碗，我们起早贪黑地忙活，甚至于透支着生命，还得洗耳恭听领导的谆谆教诲。
en: Because there are elders above and children below, and 'leaders' within the work unit besides—though we know money is not everything, we feel all the more that without money one can do nothing at all. For the children's fine future, for the health of aged parents, for the friends and family around us, for the bowl of rice in our hands, we bustle about from dawn to dusk, even overdrafting our lives, and must still listen with respectful attention to the leaders' patient instruction.

text: 人到中年，历经生活的磨难，岁月的沧桑，变得更加成熟与坚强，具备了辨别是非的能力。
en: In middle age, having weathered life's hardships and the vicissitudes of the years, we become more mature and strong, and acquire the ability to tell right from wrong.

text: 不再轻易为某句话、某件事、某个人而感动的泪流满面，除非遇到真正感人肺腑的人和事。
en: We no longer easily brim with tears of emotion over some remark, some event, or some person, unless we meet people and things that are truly touching to the heart.

text: 不会轻信他人，不再为他人的一句甜言蜜语而陶醉，也不再被他人的恶语中伤所击昏，能够做到宠辱不惊。
en: We do not readily trust others, no longer grow drunk on a few sweet words, nor are we knocked senseless by others' spiteful slanders; we can remain unperturbed by favour or disgrace.

text: 人到中年，懂得了遇事要冷静思考，多问几个“为什么”。
en: In middle age we have learnt to view matters calmly and think them through, asking ourselves a few more 'whys'.

text: 不再随心所欲，尽量控制自己的情绪。
en: We no longer follow our every whim, but try to keep our emotions in check.

text: 明白了世事难料，生活中任何事情都有可能发生。
en: We understand that the world is hard to predict, and that anything at all may happen in life.

text: 懂得了在心情激动时，做出的决定百分之九十以上是不妥当的。
en: We understand that decisions made in a surge of emotion are more than ninety per cent of the time ill-advised.

text: 相信自己，任凭风浪急，稳住钓鱼船，以不变应万变。
en: Trust yourself; though the wind and waves run high, keep the fishing boat steady, and meet ten thousand changes with the unchanging.

text: 出现问题并不可怕，可怕的是找不到解决问题的方法。
en: Problems are not frightening; what is frightening is failing to find a way to solve them.

text: 人到中年，学会了独立看人生。
en: In middle age, we learn to regard life independently.

text: 不再人云亦云，更不会随波逐流。
en: We no longer parrot others, still less drift with the tide.

text: 别人说什么并不重要，关键的是自己如何去做。
en: What others say matters little; what counts is how one conducts oneself.

text: 不再活在别人的目光里。
en: We no longer live in the gaze of others.

text: 人到中年，要的是那份踏实的生活，现实大于梦想。
en: In middle age, what one wants is that steady, settled way of living, where reality outweighs dream.

text: 也许没有梦的人生缺乏浪漫和激情，但在某些时候，红烧肉比玫瑰花更亲切。
en: Perhaps a life without dreams lacks romance and passion, but at times braised pork is dearer than roses.

text: 人到中年，懂得了只有自己心情舒畅，身体健康，才可以去照顾关爱影响别人。
en: In middle age, we understand that only when our own hearts are at ease and our bodies healthy can we care for, cherish and influence others.

text: 一个快乐的人会象磁石一样，吸引着周围的朋友。
en: A happy person attracts those around them like a magnet.

text: 与一个快乐的人在一起，自己也会变得快乐无比。
en: To be with a happy person, one's own happiness becomes boundless.

text: 体会到了人的情绪是可以传染的。
en: We come to realise that a person's mood is contagious.

text: 人到中年，有一个恬淡的心情更重要。
en: In middle age, a calm and peaceful frame of mind matters all the more.

text: 明白了人的心理健康重于身体健康。
en: We understand that mental health outweighs physical health.

text: 深知人的欲望永远没有止境，淡泊以明志，宁静而致远。
en: We know well that human desire knows no end; through indifference one's aspirations are made clear, through tranquillity one reaches afar.

text: 人到中年，也许我们的笑容更加从容、恬淡、稳重。
en: In middle age, perhaps our smiles grow more composed, calm and steady.

text: 多了思索而少了激动；多了镇定而少了浮躁；多了宽容而少了嫉妒；多了仁爱而少了仇恨。
en: There is more reflection and less excitement; more composure and less restlessness; more tolerance and less envy; more kindness and less hatred.

text: 人到中年，应该培养自己的业余爱好和兴趣：摄影、钓鱼、旅游、运动、读书、写作、电脑网络等等，这样或许会缓解一下紧张的精神负担，还可以为退休后的生活打下良好的基础，何乐而不为！
en: In middle age, one should cultivate one's hobbies and interests: photography, fishing, travel, sport, reading, writing, computers and the internet, and so on. This may ease the strained burden on the spirit, and lay a good foundation for life after retirement—why not?

text: 中年，是人生的一个必经阶段，每一个人都要长大、成熟，然后离去…
en: Middle age is a stage life must pass through; everyone must grow up, mature, and then depart…

text: 就让一切顺其自然吧。
en: Let everything take its natural course.

text: 苏东坡说得好“君子可以寓意于物，不可留意于物”，以不变应万变，心胸放宽广一些，气量放大度一些，让心灵停泊在自由宁静的港湾，生活就会过得厚重而充实。
en: Su Dongpo put it well: 'The gentleman may lodge his meaning in things, but must not fix his attention upon them.' Meet ten thousand changes with the unchanging; broaden the mind and enlarge the spirit; let the heart moor in a free and quiet harbour, and life will be lived with depth and fullness.
